'''María Isabel Mijares''' '''García-Pelayo''' (1942 – 10 February 2024) was a Spanish [[oenology|oenologist]]. She was considered the first woman in the profession and the first woman to run a winery in Spain.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |access-date=11 February 2024 |date=11 February 2024 |first=Agapito Ojosnegros |language=es |last=Lázaro |title=Fallece a los 81 años Isabel Mijares, enóloga pionera y exponente del sector del vino |url=https://www.elnortedecastilla.es/castillayleon/fallece-anos-isabel-mijares-enologa-pionera-exponente-20240211164930-nt.html |website=El Norte de Castilla}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Early life and education ==
María Isabel Mijares was born in [[Mérida, Spain|Mérida]], where she had a "happy childhood" alongside her eight siblings.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Her father's family were of [[Leonese people|Leonese]] origin, and ran a home winery, through which she was introduced to winemaking.<ref name=":2" />

Mijares began studying chemistry at [[Complutense University of Madrid|Universidad Complutense]], but put her degree on hold.<ref name=":1" /> In 1967 she began studying oenology at the Institute of Oenology of the [[University of Bordeaux]] in France after receiving a scholarship from the French government.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> While there, she met [[Émile Peynaud]], who became her mentor.<ref name=":2" /> In 1970, she completed her doctorate in oenology at the institute.<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
Mijares ran Palacio de Arganza, a winery in [[Villafranca del Bierzo]].<ref name=":1" />

From 1982 until 1987, Mijares chaired the [[Valdepeñas (DO)|Valdepeñas]] Regulatory Council, the first woman to do so. In 1985 she joined the {{ill|Royal Academy of Gastronomy|es|Real Academia de Gastronomía}} as a viticulture expert.<ref name=":1" />

From 1998 until 2019, Mijares served as the coordinator and director of the Camps Guide to the Best Wines in Spain.<ref name=":2" />

Beginning in 2017, Mijares served as technical director of wine activities for the Real Casino of Madrid.<ref name=":2" />

== Death ==
Mijares died of a heart attack in Madrid, on 10 February 2024, at the age of 81.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Cucala |first=Sara |date=11 February 2024 |title=Muere Isabel Mijares, la primera enóloga y directora de una bodega en España |url=https://elpais.com/gastronomia/2024-02-11/muere-isabel-mijares-la-primera-enologa-y-directora-de-una-bodega-en-espana.html |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=El País |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=11 February 2024 |title=Muere Isabel Mijares, primera enóloga de España y gran maestra y divulgadora del vino |url=https://www.elmundo.es/metropoli/elmundovino/2024/02/11/65c8d15121efa0516b8b457b.html |access-date=13 February 2024 |website=ELMUNDO |language=es}}</ref>
